title: What is a competency assessment?
description: A competency assessment gathers evidence to judge whether a person meets a defined workplace standard. Methods, rules of evidence and a worked example.
shortAnswer: A competency assessment is the process of gathering and judging evidence to decide whether a person can perform a task or role to a defined workplace standard. It combines evidence of performance, such as observation or work products, with evidence of the underlying knowledge, and results in a documented decision that the person is competent or not yet competent against that standard.
keyTakeaways: A competency assessment judges a person against a defined standard, not against other learners.
It needs both performance evidence (doing the task) and knowledge evidence (understanding why and when).

Regulated training systems set explicit rules: US Registered Apprenticeship standards require competencies to be tested and evaluated, and vocational regulators such as ASQA set four principles of assessment and four rules of evidence.
The decision and the evidence behind it must be recorded so that it can be reviewed, validated or challenged.

sections.heading: How does a competency assessment work?

blocks.text: A competency assessment works by comparing evidence of what a person does and knows with the requirements of a defined standard, such as a unit of competency or an entry in an organization's [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework). The assessor plans the evidence needed, collects it, judges it against the standard and records the decision.

Vocational systems publish the standards that competency assessments use. In United States Registered Apprenticeship, a competency-based program measures progress through "the individual apprentice's successful demonstration of acquired skills and knowledge, as verified by the program sponsor" ([29 CFR 29.5(b)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-A/part-29/section-29.5)). Common methods include:

items: **Direct observation** of the task in the workplace or a realiztic simulation.
**Questioning,** oral or written, to test underpinning knowledge and judgment.
**Work products,** such as completed forms, reports or built items.
**Third party reports** from supervisors, used alongside other evidence.
**Scenarios and case studies** for decisions that are rare or unsafe to rehearse live.

sections.heading: What rules make a competency assessment defensible?

blocks.text: Regulated training systems publish explicit assessment rules, and they are a useful benchmark for any organization. One detailed example is the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) [assessment practice guide](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide), which sets out Standard 1.4 of the 2025 Standards for Registered Training Organisations: assessment must follow four principles, and each assessor judgment must satisfy four rules of evidence.

blocks.caption: Principles of assessment and rules of evidence, Standard 1.4 (summarized from ASQA)
head: Item
Type
What it means in practice
rows: Accommodates learner needs, including reasonable adjustments and reassessment where necessary
Assesses relevant skills and knowledge regardless of how or where they were acquired
Includes practical application so the learner demonstrates skills in a practical setting
Evidence is interpreted consistently and outcomes are comparable across assessors
Evidence is adequate to assure the assessor the learner has the described skills and knowledge
Quality, quantity and relevance of evidence allow an informed judgment
Evidence is the learner's own original work
Evidence shows current skills and knowledge

blocks.text: ASQA's guide also notes that authenticity checks should consider whether evidence has been plagiarised or generated with artificial intelligence tools. Standard 1.5 requires assessment practices and judgments to be validated, with every training product on scope validated at least once every five years. Employers running internal assessments are not bound by these Standards, but they are a useful benchmark for defensible assessment.

Safety law sets similar expectations outside formal education. In the United States, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requires powered industrial truck training to include "evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace" ([29 CFR 1910.178(l)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XVII/part-1910/subpart-N/section-1910.178)). In the European Union, Article 12 of the [OSH Framework Directive](/regulations/eu-osh-framework-directive-training) requires adequate safety and health training specific to each worker's workstation or job, and a competency assessment is a practical way to show that standard was met.

sections.heading: How is a competency assessment different from verification of competency or an exam?

blocks.text: A competency assessment establishes whether someone meets a standard; [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) confirms that an already trained or licensed person can perform safely in a particular workplace. An exam or quiz typically measures knowledge only and is one possible input to a competency assessment, not a substitute for it.

items: [Recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning) is a competency assessment of existing evidence rather than new training.
An [assessment blueprint](/glossary/assessment-blueprint) plans which requirements each assessment task covers.
Formative checks during learning differ from the summative competency decision; see [formative vs summative assessment](/compare/formative-vs-summative-assessment).

blocks.text: Illustrative example: an assessment plan for an internal competency in a bank, "conducts customer identification for a new account".

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines assessment points in the framework before any content is written, so every competency has named evidence and a decision rule. Assessment results then attach to those points, which gives an audit trail from obligation to evidence.

faqs.q: Who can conduct a competency assessment?
faqs.a: In formal vocational systems, national rules usually specify the credentials and industry skills an assessor must hold. For internal workplace assessments, the organization sets the requirement, but good practice is an assessor who is both competent in the task and trained in assessment, so the judgment is credible if it is challenged.

faqs.q: Is a multiple choice quiz a competency assessment?
faqs.a: On its own, usually not. A quiz can provide knowledge evidence, but competency also requires evidence that the person can perform the task. ASQA's guidance on validity expects practical application components so learners demonstrate skills in a practical setting. A quiz can be one part of a wider assessment.

faqs.q: What happens when someone is assessed as not yet competent?
faqs.a: They receive feedback on which requirements were not met, further training or practice where needed, and an opportunity for reassessment. Fairness, one of the principles of assessment, explicitly includes enabling reassessment where necessary. The first result and the reassessment should both be recorded.

faqs.q: How long is a competency assessment result valid?
faqs.a: A competency decision reflects performance at a point in time. Currency is one of the rules of evidence, so older evidence carries less weight. Organizations usually set reassessment or verification intervals for high risk tasks, and trigger reassessment when a procedure, piece of equipment or regulation changes.
